html:
The Worrorra are an Aboriginal Australian people of the west Kimberley coast of Western Australia, around the islands and inlets north of King Sound. The map shows them as Worora from 1600 to 1815.

With the Ngarinyin and Wunambal they share the law of the Wandjina, the creator and rain beings whose painted faces, with eyes and no mouths, cover rock shelters in their country. Other neighbours were the Umida and Unggumi to the south.

In 1912 the Presbyterian church opened a mission on their coast, which moved to Kunmunya a few years later. In 1956 the Worrorra, Ngarinyin and Wunambal at the mission were moved to Mowanjum near Derby. The Mowanjum community became known for its Wandjina art.
sum: The Worrorra are an Aboriginal Australian people of the west Kimberley coast of Western Australia, around the islands and inlets north of King Sound. The map shows them as Worora from 1600 to 1815.
